headline: High: Continue’s filesystem/MCP defaults can ingest and act on ai-engineering-hub content, creating prompt-injection and cascading-action risk; data leakage is limited by A’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so if ai-engineering-hub content is placed in a shared workspace or fed through MCP, malicious instructions could be treated as trusted input. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and not runnable, so the pathway is inferred rather than observed, but the shared-file/MCP bridge is enough to make injection plausible.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into a workspace file that Continue reads
IF Continue is configured to consume MCP output from a source that includes untrusted text
mitigations: Keep ai-engineering-hub content in a separate read-only folder
Disable MCP servers that return untrusted text
Require manual review before any tool call triggered by file content
Use a prompt-injection scanner on imported docs
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all file and MCP inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and editor buffers and can write workspace files, but ai-engineering-hub has network_egress set to none and no data classes touched, so there is no clear path for sensitive data to leave A. The main risk is local workspace exposure rather than exfiltration, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in the same workspace that Continue can read
IF Continue is connected to a model provider that uploads editor buffers
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared workspace
Use a local-only model provider for Continue
Restrict workspace permissions to least privilege
Separate docs and code into different directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder data-class policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem and can write workspace files, so concurrent edits can conflict. ai-engineering-hub is not runnable and has no write surface, which lowers direct contention, but the shared filesystem state in Continue still creates default concurrency hazards for the pair.
conditions: IF two Continue instances edit the same workspace files
IF ai-engineering-hub artifacts are mirrored into the same filesystem tree that Continue writes to
mitigations: Open only one Continue instance per workspace
Use separate branches or directories for parallel work
Pause auto-save during coordinated edits
Review file diffs before syncing changes
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared workspace writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on MCP/tool outputs and its tool use requires user approval, but it still may treat imported content as authoritative when generating edits or actions. ai-engineering-hub’s docs can seed instructions or examples that Continue then follows, so the cascade is plausible even though the pairwise interaction is not directly documented.
conditions: IF Continue is prompted with ai-engineering-hub text as source material
IF the operator approves tool calls without verifying the originating instructions
mitigations: Require a human check before approving tool calls
Ask Continue to cite the exact source line for each action
Use a separate review step for generated edits
Limit MCP tools to read-only during analysis
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: ai-engineering-hub is open-source docs-only with no touched data classes, while Continue’s documented data classes are source code and editor buffers. There is no cited PHI, EU PII, residency, or retention mismatch in the profiles, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF PHI or regulated personal data is introduced into the shared workspace
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Document retention settings for model providers
Review data handling notices before deployment
Use local inference for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets
